title: DUSRM 0.2 Pilot — ANANTA Native Database Engine
summary: WP5 profile-reconciliation pilot. Documentation-level architecture description; not a conformance approval.

realizations.rationale: Execution budgets and exclusive writer ownership are exposed/documented in the API and transaction scope.
The engine hosts supported execution and persistence operations.
The storage subsystem owns native immutable artifacts and recovery records.
The AQL subsystem implements supported query planning and execution.
The curated embedded API exposes supported developer operations.
The engine provides the supported native database capabilities.
The native engine is the central product realization; complete platform remains in progress.

layerApplicability.rationale: The host OS provides filesystem and device I/O primitives.
ANANTA enforces resource budgets and single-writer ownership.
Supported query, ingest, scan and DDL operations execute here.
Catalog, schema snapshots, native artifacts and WAL represent persistent state.
AQL parsing/planning and analytical operators provide computation.
Embedded API and AQL are interaction boundaries.
Table, ingest, scan, query and backup/restore capabilities are exposed.
Native DBMS platform purpose is inside the model.

requirements.statement: The documented database lifecycle must enforce one exclusive writer owner and must not imply multi-writer or MVCC guarantees.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared-reference readers are scoped to the same open handle

constraints.statement: One exclusive writer owner process/handle; concurrent shared-reference readers are supported only through the same handle.
Do not claim MVCC, arbitrary multi-operation atomicity, savepoints, or general ACID semantics.
Durability claims must remain scoped to documented artifact publication and verified filesystem/platform behavior; physical power-loss immunity is not universal.

invariants.statement: For supported immutable publication operations, a durable WAL COMMIT precedes final artifact publication.
assumptions: Applies only to listed supported operations and the documented filesystem/platform scope.
invariants.method: Repository-documentation mapping; no independent crash test executed in WP5.

assertions.statement: ANANTA exposes a curated embedded Rust API with lazy AQL result iteration and versioned in-process execution budgets.

evidence.description: ANANTA README describes native engine scope, current features and limitations.
limitations: Repository claims were not independently built or tested during WP5.

evidence.description: Native engine architecture and independence boundaries.
Transaction and concurrency scope: operation-scoped atomic redo units, exclusive writer, same-handle readers; no general multi-operation ACID/MVCC.
limitations: This file conflicts with newer README claims about Windows checkpoint rotation; compatibility review remains open.

evidence.description: WAL redo/recovery specification for documented immutable artifacts and metadata operations.
limitations: The specification retains an older statement that checkpoint rotation is Unix-only; README describes targeted Windows replacement support.

evidence.description: Embedded API contract v0.1 describes typed errors, lazy result iteration, execution budgets and cancellation.
limitations: M7.1 remains in progress; this is not a stable network protocol.

evidence.description: Optional privacy-minimized file-based FireBot JSONL workload connector.
limitations: File-based workload only; no live FireBot DB connection or production telemetry integration is established.
